name: Soviet anti-Zionism
summary: Soviet anti-Zionism was the official Marxist-Leninist campaign, strongest from 1967 to the mid-1980s, that treated Zionism as the ideology of the wealthy Jewish bourgeoisie allied with imperialist monopoly capital, as chauvinist, racist and anti-communist, and as an enemy of national liberation. It backed the Arab states and the Palestinian cause, favoured the assimilation of Jews where they live over a Jewish state, accepted Israel's existence while demanding its withdrawal from occupied land, and ran alongside state atheism and restrictions on Jewish emigration. Scholars describe much of its propaganda as antisemitic, which Soviet officials denied.
scope: The official CPSU line from Lenin's rejection of Zionism through the post-1967 Brezhnev-era propaganda campaign, based on Yuri Ivanov's Caution: Zionism! (1969), the Great Soviet Encyclopedia entry and the 'Zionology' literature (Kichko, Begun). It excludes Stalin's brief pro-Israel policy of 1944-48 and Western leftist anti-Zionism after the USSR. Because it is an ideology of one issue set inside Marxism-Leninism, the many answers on unrelated questions are inferred from Soviet state doctrine and practice, and marked low.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet state's guaranteed free medical care; the sources do not discuss health policy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: a state-wage system with a guaranteed minimum; raises were policy, but the sources are silent.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Ivanov treats the capitalist order as the base of the imperialist, anti-communist forces he attacks; Marxism-Leninism prefers planning.

public-ownership.rationale: Ivanov writes from the standpoint of the first workers' and peasants' state, where all major industry was state-owned.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from hostility to the wealthy Jewish bourgeoisie and monopoly circles; private fortunes had no legitimate place in the USSR.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: Soviet unions existed as party-led bodies for workers, but their independence was not a Soviet aim.

property-fundamental.rationale: Zionism is defined as the politics of the wealthy bourgeoisie allied to monopoly capital; private property in production is the thing opposed.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: Ivanov condemns monopoly circles, but the Soviet answer was abolition of corporations, not regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet commitment to state-guaranteed social provision and its attack on capitalist inequality.

worker-ownership.rationale: Soviet doctrine held production to be owned by the whole people through the state rather than by workers firm by firm.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The KGB sponsored the campaign and the Soviet security state routinely watched citizens; it called Israel a terrorist regime.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the puritanical, prohibitionist Soviet state; the sources are silent.

state-harmful.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds the state is needed until communism; Ivanov defends the Soviet state against its enemies.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: private firearm ownership was tightly restricted in the USSR.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Ivanov treats anti-communism as the enemy, and Soviet doctrine rejected equating communism with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist historiography treats slavery as the basis of the conflict; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Soviet practice removed monuments of the old order; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Soviet doctrine held universal laws of historical stages; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The party, not the army, was guardian of order; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Soviet doctrine socialised care in nurseries rather than paying domestic work; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Soviet law obliged adult children to support disabled parents; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: The party nomenklatura, not exams, controlled office; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The USSR had a state monopoly on foreign trade and bar to foreign ownership; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Soviet divorce was comparatively easy after the 1960s; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution favoured recallable officials; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Soviet pensions were state-paid; private accounts opposed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land was state property under the Soviet constitution, used by farms and individuals.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Supreme Soviet formally approved the budget; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Russian was lingua franca but republics had their own languages; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership of land was impossible in the USSR; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Doctrine neither addresses nor settles the legal question; adherents are split between structural and formal equality.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Soviet propaganda criticised Western consumerism; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The USSR armed Arab states and allied liberation forces; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Brezhnev Doctrine justified action in allied states; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Ivanov charges monopoly circles with steering the policies of the imperialist powers.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Ivanov portrays Zionist funds as an imperialist instrument; the USSR banned foreign funding of civil groups.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Soviet family policy gave benefits to mothers of large families; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: The propiska system tied housing to residence permits; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Full employment was a constitutional right of Soviet citizens.

democratic-peace.rationale: Ivanov treats imperialist democracies as warmongers.

non-intervention.rationale: Soviet rhetoric stressed non-interference while supplying allies; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Soviet unions were organised by branch of industry; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Scholars say Soviet anti-Zionist literature echoed the Protocols, alleging an international Zionist conspiracy, though the official line denied antisemitism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Soviet law kept marriage as a registered institution; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: State secrecy and censorship were the rule; inferred.

local-production.rationale: The USSR planned for specialised and large-scale production; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The party demanded organisation under its own leadership.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Soviet law stressed state sovereignty; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Ivanov denies Jews are a nation defined by religion; Soviet doctrine rejects religious nationhood.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Soviet doctrine disavowed tribute, though bloc states deferred to Moscow; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Central planning redistributed revenue between regions; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Soviet doctrine permitted personal property for everyday goods.

defeat-communism.rationale: Ivanov names anti-communism as the core of Zionism; communism's defeat is the enemy's aim.

religion-illusion.rationale: Scientific atheism held religion to be a product of oppression; Kichko's book attacked Judaism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Ivanov credits the age of capitalism with breaking down the ghetto walls, in line with the Marxist view.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Soviet doctrine held that women's emancipation follows the socialist transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Soviet policy expanded nurseries and canteens; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: Soviet law honoured treaties formally.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Utopian small communes were opposed in favour of state socialism; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ivanov condemns Zionist settlement of Palestinian land; inferred for majority settlement elsewhere.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ivanov defends communism against all alternatives.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Ivanov devotes chapters to rebutting the claim that historic Jewish ties to Palestine justify a Jewish state.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The USSR officially recognised the Nazi genocide, though propaganda tended to downplay Jewish specificity and compare Israel to the Nazis.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Soviet law punished anti-Soviet agitation; the state curbed Jewish organisations.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Soviet doctrine attacked religion, so protecting it from blasphemy is opposed.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The USSR backed Arab states as political actors, not on religious grounds; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Official doctrine praised mass participation in soviets; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Class was primary in Soviet doctrine; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; Soviet conservatism on gender; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Ivanov frames Marxism-Leninism against reaction; the notion of a synthesis is rejected.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's theory of alienation is not stressed in Soviet doctrine; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The USSR allied itself with Muslim Arab states.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The secular Soviet state discouraged religious symbols in institutions; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ivanov calls the socialist system superior to capitalist adaptations.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The USSR maintained huge forces and armed Arab states.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The USSR led one bloc and pressed Arab states to side with it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary rule is contrary to Soviet doctrine.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: state banking replaced mutual credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Soviet doctrine opposed IMF-style conditions as imperialist; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Soviet doctrine considers property franchises a bourgeois device.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism was not part of Soviet doctrine; inferred.

reification.rationale: Lukacs's concept was not Soviet orthodoxy, so the adherent view is split or unaddressed.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Ivanov claims Zionist and imperialist money controls Western media and the means of opinion.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Socialist legality claimed published laws; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The USSR condemned racial restrictions on the vote.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the party controlled participation; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: The Soviet state kept official information secret; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Soviet civil law ignored religious restrictions on marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Official doctrine opposed any ethnic or religious boycott; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The party guided participation, not random assemblies; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Soviet doctrine called religion reactionary and not reformable; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ivanov traces Zionist and imperialist power to concentrated monopoly wealth.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Soviet policy promoted scientific atheism, and Kichko's book was published by a state academy.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Soviet state sustained a large police and penal system; withering of the state was deferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Soviet doctrine favoured a unitary party-led federation; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from Soviet doctrine, which treated social provision as a state duty and private charity as a bourgeois palliative.

term-limits.rationale: Soviet office-holders had no term limits, though the system formally had elections; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Soviet voters formally elected deputies who were subject to recall, not delegating topic by topic; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Soviet propaganda made preventing nuclear war a leading cause, but the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Soviet doctrine stressed equality of women while opposing religion; equal eligibility is inferred, with little interest in religious offices.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Soviet family law declared spouses equal; inferred from state doctrine, not from the sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from Soviet practice, which reserved voting to citizens of the Soviet state.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet state's fixed low rents under state housing; the sources do not discuss housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet state's retention of copyright and inventor certificates; the sources do not discuss it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the Pioneers and Komsomol as state-run organised youth movements with military-patriotic training.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from Soviet nuclear forces on its own territory; the sources do not discuss it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The USSR attacked Western bases abroad, though it kept forces in allied states; inferred from the Cold War line.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from Soviet commemoration of Nazi crimes, though it avoided singling out Jewish victims.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marxism-Leninism's socialist principle was reward by work done, and Ivanov attacks Jewish capital as parasitic ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from Soviet doctrine of just wars and defence of the socialist fatherland.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ivanov follows Lenin in denying a continuous Jewish nation, and Marxism treats nations as historical products.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from Soviet orthodoxy, which treated sex differences as natural; not discussed in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from Soviet class-first approach to women's questions; not discussed in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: State atheism rejected saints, though the war dead were honoured as heroes; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marxist-Leninist materialism rejects spiritual explanations of politics; politics is class struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Ivanov rejected gathering Jews in Israel and favoured assimilation, but the cultural-centre idea is not addressed.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist priority of class struggle and the state over cultural nationalism; Ivanov attacks Zionism's cultural claims.

god-not-male.rationale: State atheism implies no theology of God; no position on gendered language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Soviet doctrine treated religion as a relic to be overcome, not reformed; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Official doctrine opposed national privilege, and Ivanov cites Lenin against Zionist chauvinism of one people over others.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Soviet federalism had ethnic units, including a Jewish Autonomous Oblast, but no stated position on merging regions.

independent-unions.rationale: Soviet unions were run as transmission belts of the Communist Party, not independent bodies.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine holds that socialism requires working-class (proletarian) political power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from state ownership of services in the Soviet system.

second-chamber.rationale: The Supreme Soviet had two chambers, one representing nationalities; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Soviet doctrine favoured state and collective-farm ownership, not municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Democratic centralism rejected decentralised confederal decisions.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Soviet claims to guarantee workers a livable wage; not addressed directly.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet state's insistence on control of money and information.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from Soviet control of communication and identity.

person-over-state.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine put the collective and party above the individual.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Official Marxism-Leninism was materialist and atheist and hostile to religious spirituality.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the unitary Soviet state's central authority over republics and regions.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from Soviet faith in technological and scientific progress.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The campaign condemned Zionism as racist nationalism and favoured class over ethnic organising.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from Soviet internationalism, which treated ethnic and racial pride as chauvinism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from official Soviet claims that its military was for defence only.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet (Stalinist) definition of a nation as a community of language, territory, economic life and culture, applied by the campaign to deny Jews were one nation; sources do not state it directly.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: Soviet doctrine opposed religious-communal political bodies, ran state atheism and favoured assimilation of Jews where they live, so separate religious electorates would be rejected.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Soviet propaganda framed Zionism and imperialism as plotting against the USSR and the Arab states, and Ivanov describes Zionist subversion; applied to partition of one's country this is inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from Soviet state education, where higher education was free and students received stipends; the sources do not discuss it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: Soviet planning relied on state direction and regulation, not pricing mechanisms, and the sources are silent on environmental policy.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from Soviet official rhetoric on building socialism for coming generations; the sources do not discuss ecology.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: official Soviet doctrine stressed formal equality of women and men and treated gender-specific political values with suspicion; sources are silent.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: the USSR publicly campaigned for disarmament and peace while building up forces, so adherents would endorse reduction in principle; the sources cover the Arab arms supply rather than disarmament.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Lenin's 1917 Decree on Peace denounced secret treaties, but Soviet practice was secretive; the sources do not settle which an adherent would affirm.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet state monopoly of foreign trade and currency, which barred private cross-border capital movement; the sources do not discuss it.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet party-state's monopoly on armed force; the sources do not discuss private arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist doctrine, which backed defence of the Soviet state and 'just' wars and punished refusal; the sources do not discuss conscientious refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from Soviet trade unions signing collective agreements with enterprise management, though they were state-run; the sources do not cover labour relations.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from a system of guaranteed state employment and wages that had no tax top-ups; the sources are silent on this.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from a planned economy in which the budget followed the central plan rather than legal borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from Soviet support for developing countries and national liberation against imperialist economic control.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's State and Revolution, which Soviet doctrine applied to bourgeois states; the sources do not discuss it directly.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from central planning under a single fixed blueprint of socialist construction.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from Soviet planning that did not price nature as capital and criticised bourgeois commodification; the sources are silent.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from state atheism and proletarian internationalism, which treated the nation as no sacred community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from free Soviet higher education with stipends, so graduates carried no student loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the official doctrine that the Soviet nationalities were in a friendship of peoples without exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist view that human nature is shaped by social conditions and from the aim of a new Soviet man.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from Party control of all Soviet press and broadcasting, which was neither independent nor commercial.

religions-one-truth.rationale: State atheism treated all religions as false ideology, so the claim that all express one spiritual truth is rejected; the sources note anti-Zionism ran alongside state atheism.

farm-price-support.rationale: Soviet doctrine favoured state-controlled collective farm procurement and fixed prices; inferred from Soviet state practice, as the sources do not discuss it.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The USSR kept and expanded its nuclear arsenal against the West and called disarmament conditional on mutual agreement; inferred from state practice.

workers-own-party.rationale: Under the CPSU's single-party doctrine, independent workers' parties were rejected, as the party claimed to be the sole workers' vanguard; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Soviet law declared women equal and the Soviet state opposed such practices as backward customs; inferred, as the sources do not discuss FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Soviet law formally guaranteed women equal rights with men in property and inheritance, and the state presented this as a proud achievement; documented in Soviet doctrine on women's equality, inferred for this audit.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Soviet linguistics was dominated by nationality policy distinguishing separate national languages; adherents had no unified view and the sources are silent.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Soviet doctrine had no private property in industrial land, and pollution was handled by state planning agencies; the sources do not discuss it, so inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Soviet doctrine rejected hereditary and traditional authority in lawmaking in favour of party and soviet institutions; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Soviet practice put heavy industrial growth ahead of the environment, though it also declared nature conservation a state task; adherents' view is mixed and inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Soviet criminal law centralised punishment under the state with strict fixed penalties for serious crimes; inferred from state practice.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Soviet policy promoted Russian as the language of interethnic communication; inferred, as the sources do not discuss immigration language rules.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Soviet trade unions were state-run bodies that nearly all workers joined; inferred from Soviet labour practice, the sources do not discuss it.

voter-id.rationale: Soviet elections were uncontested single-list votes with near-universal turnout; no stated position on identification requirements.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: State atheism treated religion as obsolete and restricted all of it, including Judaism; the official line favoured no recognised interpretation, but not equal legal standing either; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine defined democracy by class content and the party's leading role, not by competitive elections; inferred from Soviet state doctrine.

premarital-sex.rationale: Official Soviet moral doctrine was austere in practice while legally permissive; split and not addressed in the sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; the Soviet state censored and jammed information freely for order, so shutdowns are inferred to be acceptable.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Soviet doctrine rejected cash-transfer substitutes for state provision and planned employment; inferred from Marxist-Leninist practice.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Soviet state claimed full legal equality and women's suffrage from 1917 and the official line presented this as a Soviet achievement.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marxist-Leninist atheism held religion to be a tool of oppression, women's included; inferred from Soviet doctrine.

race-social-construct.rationale: Soviet doctrine denounced racial theories as bourgeois pseudoscience and equated Zionism with racism; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The Soviet Union had the Zhenotdel early and the Soviet Women's Committee later, but not a ministry in the modern sense; the sources do not discuss it.

missingStatements.text: Jews are a religious community, not a nation, and have no claim to a state of their own.
missingStatements.rationale: Ivanov rejects the Zionist idea of a world Jewish nation and cites Lenin on the assimilation of Jews into the nations among which they live.

missingStatements.text: Zionism is a form of racism.
missingStatements.rationale: The Soviet line, backed by the USSR's sponsorship of UN General Assembly Resolution 3379 in 1975, defined Zionism as racist chauvinism.

missingStatements.text: A state should withdraw from territory it occupied in war, and the country's refugees should be allowed to return, as a condition of settling a conflict.
missingStatements.rationale: Ivanov's proposed settlement demands withdrawal of Israeli forces from the occupied Arab lands and recognition of the Arab refugees' rights.

missingStatements.text: Movements that organise a national minority separately from the working class serve the ruling class.
missingStatements.rationale: Ivanov applies Lenin's critique of the Bund to Zionist efforts to pull Jewish workers away from the class struggle.

notes: Scholars (cited in s2 and s4) describe much of the 1967-85 propaganda as antisemitic and as echoing the Protocols; Soviet officials denied this. The answer on minority-conspiracy follows that documented content, while the official line framed its target as international Zionism. Before 1991 the USSR acknowledged Israel's existence; the profile does not extend to Stalin's 1947-48 pro-Israel line.
